channel.title: The Melbourne Indian
channel.description: Independent, free-to-read news for Melbourne's Indian communities in English, Hindi and Punjabi.

item.title: From Saturday, new visitor visas come with a 'No Further Stay' condition. Here is what it means for parents, partners and students
item.description: Every visitor visa, ETA and eVisitor applied for from 28 November will carry condition 8503. Holders will not be able to lodge most visa applications from inside Australia unless the condition is waived.

item.title: Flight Centre data breach: passport details among customer records that may have been accessed
item.description: Unknown people may have reached a 'significant number' of records in a booking system used by Flight Centre, Travel Associates and Cruiseabout. Here is what was exposed, and what to do if you have booked a holiday.

item.title: Final costings: what Labor and the Coalition say they would spend, save and sell
item.description: Both major parties released the costings of their promises on Thursday, two days before Saturday's election. Here are the key numbers from each.

item.title: Punjab's Gurnoor Brar makes his Test debut as India bowl first in the Christchurch decider
item.description: Shubman Gill won the toss in the second and final Test against New Zealand. Brar, born in Muktsar, replaces Prasidh Krishna, and India need a win for their first series victory in New Zealand since 2009.

item.title: Victoria votes tomorrow: early voting closes at 6pm today, and more than 1.9 million have already voted
item.description: Polls are open from 8am to 6pm on Saturday. Here is what to do if your postal vote has not arrived, how to fill in both ballot papers so your vote counts, and where to get help in Hindi and Punjabi.

item.title: Starting a business in Melbourne: the steps, and the extra rules for builders and tradies
item.description: From an ABN to builder registration and Victoria's new Home Warranty insurance, here is what the law asks of you before your first job, and where to get free help.

item.title: New community register counts thousands of anti-Hindu comments online, refers threats to police
item.description: The Melbourne-based pilot says it has logged hateful comments on public social media threads about temples, Diwali and a Hindu school, and passed threats to Victoria Police.

item.title: SkillSelect moves into ImmiAccount on 28 November: what skilled visa hopefuls need to know
item.description: Submitted Expressions of Interest stay valid, but unfinished drafts will not carry over. Here is what changes for 189, 190 and 491 applicants.

item.title: India chase a first Test series win in New Zealand for 17 years as the decider starts in Christchurch on Friday
item.description: The two-match series is level after the Wellington draw. Play at Hagley Oval starts at 9am Melbourne time on Friday, at a ground where fast bowlers take most of the wickets.

item.title: Going home for Christmas on a bridging visa? Expect closer scrutiny of travel requests from 30 November
item.description: If you are waiting on a 482, 186 or 494 visa and need to leave Australia, a vague reason like 'holiday' may no longer get you a long travel window.

item.title: Final polls put Coalition ahead and One Nation second, as a YouGov model projects Carroll losing his seat
item.description: Two days before the Victorian election, Resolve Strategic has the Coalition on 31 per cent, One Nation 25 and Labor 20. A YouGov seat model published by the Herald Sun projects Premier Ben Carroll losing Niddrie.

item.title: More than 1.65 million Victorians have voted early, after a third record day in a row
item.description: The Victorian Electoral Commission recorded 272,312 early votes on Wednesday, the busiest day yet. Early voting closes at 6pm on Friday, and election day is Saturday.

item.title: North Melbourne and Melbourne to meet in first Friday-night AFLW grand final
item.description: North Melbourne chase a third straight flag against Melbourne at IKON Park on Friday night. Tickets start at $35.

item.title: Liberal frontbencher Leah Blyth defects to One Nation, giving Hanson her first South Australian senator
item.description: The former SA Liberal president says she can no longer tell Australians the Liberal Party can save the country. Her move comes two days before a Victorian election in which One Nation is polling second.

item.title: The other ballot paper: what to know about Victoria's upper house on Saturday
item.description: The larger ballot paper needs at least five numbers, group voting tickets are gone, and analysts expect a very different Legislative Council after 28 November.

item.title: Inflation jumps to 4.9%, the highest since 2023, as power and petrol prices soar
item.description: Annual inflation rose more than economists expected in October, driven by electricity and fuel. Prices in Melbourne rose 4.4 per cent. The Reserve Bank meets again on 7 and 8 December.

item.title: Struggling with mortgage repayments? How to ask your lender for hardship help
item.description: Lenders must consider a request for hardship help. Here is what to say, what they can offer and where to get free advice.

item.title: Roy Morgan poll has Coalition ahead 55-45 in Victoria in the final week, with One Nation on 20 per cent
item.description: Labor's primary vote is unchanged at 22.5 per cent in the SMS poll of 1,563 Victorians, while One Nation slipped two points.

item.title: Medicine prices frozen: PBS scripts to stay at $25 until the end of the decade
item.description: The Albanese government will legislate to stop the usual yearly rise in PBS co-payments, at a cost of about $242 million.

item.title: Melbourne is Australia's second most affordable capital for renters, but students and low-paid workers still struggle
item.description: A new national index finds rents are at their least affordable since 2012. Melbourne fares better than most capitals, but share-housing students, hospitality workers and pensioners are still stretched.

item.title: Guru Nanak Gurpurab is here: what the day means and how Melbourne's Sikhs mark it
item.description: India's official holiday list puts the first Sikh Guru's birth anniversary on Tuesday 24 November, though some calendars give Wednesday. Gurdwaras hold special programmes and langar.

item.title: Mitchell and Phillips bat out the final session as New Zealand hold India to a draw in Wellington
item.description: India declared on 720/9 and took three wickets on the last day, but could not break Daryl Mitchell and Glenn Phillips after tea at the Basin Reserve. The second Test starts in Christchurch on Friday.

item.title: David Jones tells 1,689 staff their jobs will end on 30 December
item.description: Workers at the 19 stores being closed, including Highpoint, Glen Waverley and Malvern Central, received redundancy notices on Friday. The retail union says only about one in 10 will be offered another role.

item.title: Two teens charged with affray after man, 21, dies in La Trobe Street stabbing
item.description: Five young men were arrested over the death of a Narre Warren man in Melbourne's CBD on Saturday night. Three have been released pending further inquiries.

item.title: Final week: experts tip a heavy Labor loss as Victoria heads to Saturday's election
item.description: Political scientists and poll analysts say the Coalition is on track for majority government. Both leaders say every vote counts, and nothing is decided until Saturday.

item.title: Inflation tipped to hit 4.7%, a three-year high, when October figures land on Wednesday
item.description: Fuel and electricity are driving prices up, economists say, and October is the first month to show the effect of the card surcharge ban. The ABS releases the figures at 11.30am Wednesday.

item.title: Flying to India this summer? Victoria's health chief says get hepatitis A and measles protection first
item.description: The Chief Health Officer names India among the countries where travellers should be vaccinated against hepatitis A, and says to see a doctor six to eight weeks before you go.

item.title: 70 years since Melbourne's Olympics: India's sixth hockey gold, and farewell to swimming champion Jon Henricks
item.description: The Games opened at the MCG on 22 November 1956. India won hockey gold without conceding a goal, and one of Australia's home heroes has died aged 91.

item.title: Australia and China agree to hold talks on artificial intelligence as Albanese ends 11-day trip
item.description: The dialogue was agreed when Anthony Albanese met Premier Li Qiang in Beijing, days after Australia and India signed a US-led pact on AI supply chains.

item.title: A fifth Melbourne Cup is missing: Frank Reys's 1973 trophy was stolen from Flemington years ago, ABC reveals
item.description: The cup won by Gala Supreme, ridden by the first Indigenous jockey to win the race, was taken from a display at the racecourse and never recovered. A relative of Gala Supreme's trainer says security was 'lax'.
